svg.title: A Thirty-Day Evidence-to-Submission Sprint
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-08-thirty-day-launch-sprint; chart type: timeline_roadmap; title: A Thirty-Day Evidence-to-Submission Sprint; subtitle: Build an authorized pilot before expanding claim volume; chapter number: 12; epistemic tag: operating_framework; assumptions note: Milestones are operator-controlled launch deliverables, not promised refund dates. The canonical time to first deal is 1-4 months; municipal refunds, assessment appeals, and tax-credit certification can take longer than this sprint.; caption: Finish the month with traceable pilot evidence, tested fee math, and a documented submission or a specific remediation plan; do not substitute projected recoveries for collected revenue.; stages: label: Days 1-7; value: Define one lane and secure the workspace; numeric value: 7.0; detail: Choose one customer profile and recovery lane. Review applicable contract terms, tax-service scope, or state credentials; prepare authority and fee documents. Configure encrypted storage, individual accounts, access logging, and a deadline register.; label: Days 8-14; value: Secure a pilot and preserve baseline evidence; numeric value: 14.0; detail: Conduct targeted outreach and seek one authorized pilot. After signature, obtain invoice and payment records and preserve their original versions. If no pilot signs, continue acquisition and test the workflow with synthetic records without claiming client access or recoveries.; label: Days 15-21; value: Validate exceptions and calculate the fee basis; numeric value: 21.0; detail: Reconcile extracted records against source documents, remove duplicates, test eligibility, and calculate supported claim amounts. Review waivers, tariff periods, credentials, or WOTC timing as applicable. Have a second qualified reviewer inspect material exceptions.; label: Days 22-30; value: Submit supported claims and establish reconciliation; numeric value: 30.0; detail: Submit only authorized, eligible pilot matters and store acceptance receipts. If evidence remains incomplete, issue a dated remediation list instead. Build refund-to-invoice matching, aging reports, shared-savings baseline checks, and a fee ledger that separates pending value from earned revenue.

rect.title: label: Days 1-7; value: Define one lane and secure the workspace; numeric value: 7.0; detail: Choose one customer profile and recovery lane. Review applicable contract terms, tax-service scope, or state credentials; prepare authority and fee documents. Configure encrypted storage, individual accounts, access logging, and a deadline register.

rect.title: label: Days 8-14; value: Secure a pilot and preserve baseline evidence; numeric value: 14.0; detail: Conduct targeted outreach and seek one authorized pilot. After signature, obtain invoice and payment records and preserve their original versions. If no pilot signs, continue acquisition and test the workflow with synthetic records without claiming client access or recoveries.

rect.title: label: Days 15-21; value: Validate exceptions and calculate the fee basis; numeric value: 21.0; detail: Reconcile extracted records against source documents, remove duplicates, test eligibility, and calculate supported claim amounts. Review waivers, tariff periods, credentials, or WOTC timing as applicable. Have a second qualified reviewer inspect material exceptions.

rect.title: label: Days 22-30; value: Submit supported claims and establish reconciliation; numeric value: 30.0; detail: Submit only authorized, eligible pilot matters and store acceptance receipts. If evidence remains incomplete, issue a dated remediation list instead. Build refund-to-invoice matching, aging reports, shared-savings baseline checks, and a fee ledger that separates pending value from earned revenue.

Assumptions: Milestones are operator-controlled launch deliverables, not promised refund dates. The canonical time to first deal is 1-4 months; municipal refunds, assessment appeals, and tax-credit certification can take longer than this sprint.
